What I can't stand is repetitive admin like filing, data entry or following rigid checklists.

query_sentences: During my internship last summer I was mostly analysing data and checking results, so maybe it sounds like I only like research because that's what I happened to do. I get quite satisfied when everything is neatly organised and documented. Building or fixing small things can be fun once in a while too. But I don't enjoy having to support or counsel people all day. Persuading people or selling ideas really isn't my thing either.

Nothing satisfies me more than turning a messy spreadsheet into perfect order, with every record checked and every step of the process clearly laid out. I also really like leading a team and persuading people to back a plan, like when our CCA had to convince the school to approve a bigger budget. Working out why the numbers don't add up is genuinely fun for me too. On the other hand, hands-on work with tools, engines or wiring is something I really don't like.

I enjoy keeping things orderly and making sure details are right. I'm not big on persuading people or selling things. Creative work like drawing or designing is something I really don't enjoy.

The thing that excites me most is persuading people and running the show; selling merch at our hall's flea market and smashing our sales target was such a rush. Helping friends out when they're stuck is kinda nice too. Keeping things neat and orderly is fine, I guess. But please, nothing hands-on with tools, machines or outdoor physical work, because that really isn't me.

query_sentences: My dad handles the accounts for his company and I help him at year-end, and honestly I really like it, because keeping records accurate and organised is so satisfying. I keep detailed spreadsheets for everything in my own life too. Following clear procedures and getting the details right is what I'm best at. Hands-on physical work like fixing things or building stuff is not for me though.

Being there for people is what matters most to me; I volunteer weekly at a tuition programme for kids from lower-income families and it's the highlight of my week. I'm also really curious about why people behave the way they do, and I like reading studies and testing ideas. Sales pitching or pushing people to buy things isn't really my style. And detailed admin, like updating records and following procedures to the letter, really drains me.

But hands-on stuff with tools, machines or outdoor physical labour I really dislike.

source_evidence.text: Helping people is what I care about most, I volunteer at a community centre and love it. I'm also curious about why people think the way they do. Keeping track of records and paperwork is something I really dislike. Hands-on technical work isn't really my thing either. Sorting records and doing paperwork is honestly one of my favourite things.

Taking charge and negotiating are what get me most excited; I used to resell sneakers online and haggling to close deals was a total rush. I'm also really into organising, like keeping meticulous records of my stock and expenses in spreadsheets. Planning a tight schedule for group projects is satisfying too. Drawing or art projects aren't really my cup of tea.

source_evidence.text: What gets me most excited is pitching an idea and convincing people to get on board; last semester I rallied sponsors for our hall's fundraising drive and closing each deal was the highlight. I also like taking charge of a group project and pushing the team toward a goal. Digging into data to understand a problem is kinda fun too. But anything hands-on with tools or fixing machines is really not for me, and I'd hate spending my day assembling or repairing things.

I enjoy taking charge, convincing people and seeing a plan come together because I pushed it through. I don't mind keeping things organised either. My course has a lot of lab and workshop components with equipment, and since I've already done so many of those I figure I should go into something along those lines. Designing or doing artsy things isn't really for me.

Working out why the numbers don't add up is genuinely fun for me too. On the other hand, hands-on work with tools, engines or wiring is something I really don't like.

I'm also really into helping people, whether it's tutoring juniors or listening to friends when they're stressed. Figuring out why something works is kinda interesting too. I'm not too keen on fiddly hands-on stuff like assembling furniture though.

I really enjoy working through tough problems and analysing data until things make sense. I also like keeping my notes and files well organised. I enjoy being the one who leads and persuades the group. Having to lead people or persuade them is something I really dislike. I'd much rather focus on the work itself than pitch it to anyone.
